newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: UK buy boosts DBS Land hotel arm.
newsitem.headline: UK buy boosts DBS Land hotel arm.

text.p: DBS Land Ltd's move to buy a London hotel for Singapore $105 million was a strategic move to boost its hotel operations, analysts said on Monday.
Through subsidiary Raffles Holdings Pte Ltd, the group bought Brown's Hotel, a 19th century hotel in the prestigeous Mayfair district, from Britain's Granada Group Plc on Friday.
"It is part of the group's ongoing strategy to expand its hotel arm," Lim Chung Chun, investment analyst with ING Baring Securities, told Reuters.

Brown's, one of London's oldest and most established hotels, boasting of famous guests ranging back to U.S. President Theodore Roosevelt and inventor Alexander Graham Bell, would enhance Raffles' position in luxury hotels with historical links, analysts said.
Raffles is slated for a listing in Singapore this year.
DBS Land owns 56.67 percent of Raffles Hotel in Singapore and operates two hotels, located at historical sites, in Cambodia.
It also has a 30 percent stake in Raffles City, 100 percent stake in Merchant Court Hotel and two country clubs in Singapore.
For the financial year ended December 31, 1996, its pre-tax profit after interest from hotel operations was at S$30.42 million, 13.8 percent of the group's pre-tax profit.

Analysts were confident DBS Land, which made a 91.9 million share placement on June 3 to partly finance its S$391 million purchase of a 19.2 percent stake in healthcare company Parkway Holdings, should be able to finance its latest acquisition comfortably.
Some expected the group, with a 70:30 debt-equity ratio, to sell some of its non-core property investments in Singapore to meet its cash requirements.
They said they would not be adjusting their earnings forecasts for DBS Land.
"S$105 million won't pose any problem for DBS Land. If they do mount a takeover for Parkway, it will raise their gearing to over 100 percent. But it will still be manageable for them," said Lim.
DBS Land's net earnings for the year ending December 31, 1997 were forecast at S$253-257 million. Its earnings per share growth is projected at 16-18 percent from 22.5 cents last year.

For the year ending December 31, 1998, analysts expected earnings to go beyond S$310 million, spurred by contributions from a condominium development in Singapore as well as developments in Hong Kong.
